_about: Auto-detect the render mode (flat / single-sheet-block-diagram / multi-sheet-hierarchy) from the user's natural-language prompt when the agent did NOT pass an explicit force_hierarchy / force_single_sheet flag. Decision order: (1) explicit prompt phrases win, (2) recommended-block count from sheet_planner_rules.json drives a threshold-based pick, (3) fall through to engine size-based auto. Everything tunable in JSON.

block_count_thresholds._doc: Number of distinct functional blocks (from sheet_planner.recommend_blocks(prompt)) that pushes the auto-decision into each tier. MUST stay aligned with layout_config.json:sheet_decision.single_sheet_max_blocks (=5): SINGLE_SHEET_BLOCKS holds 3-5 functional groups on ONE A3 sheet; 6+ groups go HIERARCHY. Set 2026-06-03 to match the engine override (n_blk > 5 -> hierarchy) so the pre-architect decision, the architect's block emission, and the user-facing render_mode_decision all agree instead of the engine silently re-deciding post-architect.

component_estimate_signals._doc: Optional secondary signal: rough component-count contribution per keyword. Summed and combined with the block count. Helps catch dense circuits whose keyword footprint is large even if block count is small (e.g. esp32 + lora + display = 30+ parts under 3 blocks).

complexity_thresholds._doc: Same decision as block_count_thresholds, but on the sum-of-keyword-weights instead of distinct-block-count. Raised 2026-06-02 from 40/15 to 65/12 because a typical USB-C STM32 dev board (the user's reference image) scores ~40 complexity but belongs in single-sheet-block-diagram --- not hierarchy. Hierarchy is reserved for genuinely dense designs (multi-MCU + many peripherals).

_decision_logic_doc: HIERARCHY: blocks >= hierarchy_when_blocks_at_least OR complexity >= hierarchy_when_complexity_at_least. EITHER strong signal is enough -- dense circuits need multi-sheet even if block names are sparse, and many distinct functional groups need multi-sheet even at lower density. SINGLE_SHEET_BLOCKS: blocks >= single_sheet_blocks_when_blocks_at_least AND complexity >= single_sheet_blocks_when_complexity_at_least. BOTH must agree -- block-count alone over-promotes simple discrete circuits (USB lamp keyword hits 4 blocks but only ~9 parts), complexity alone over-promotes single-IC dense circuits (MCU + many passives, no real groups). FLAT (default): everything below the SINGLE_SHEET_BLOCKS thresholds -- discrete circuits like USB lamps, NE555 blinkers, single op-amp filters, single LDOs.
